messages:
Sam H: Hey team — seeing a weird gap in traces for our Celery background workers. Root request span shows up in Tempo/Grafana, but most child spans created inside tasks are missing. Anyone run into this with the Python OTEL SDK?

Olivia M: @Sam H can you paste how you initialise the tracer in the worker boot? Common issue: tracer provider not set up in the worker process (noop tracer) or init happening after tasks start.

Sam H: Sure, startup snippet we run in the worker process:
```python
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor, OTLPSpanExporter
from opentelemetry.propagate import set_global_textmap
from opentelemetry.propagators.ottrace import TraceContextTextMapPropagator

provider = TracerProvider()
trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)
exporter = OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint="https://otlp.collector.internal:4317")
provider.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(exporter))
set_global_textmap(TraceContextTextMapPropagator())
```
We also set env vars: `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=traceidratio` and `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG=0.05`.

Olivia M: A few quick checks: 1) make sure this init runs in the worker main process (Celery forks can inherit state weirdly). 2) env sampler name varies by SDK; `traceidratio` is the env shorthand, but confirm the SDK version supports it. 3) BatchSpanProcessor + short-lived worker processes can drop spans if the process exits before flush — call `shutdown()` or `force_flush()` on worker shutdown.

Nate R: Also check the collector/agent sampling. Our otel-collector has a sampling processor for head-based sampling that can drop spans before export. Example snippet from collector config: 
```yaml
processors:
  sampling/svc_celery:
    decision_wait: 2s
    hash_seed: 22
    policies:
      - name: default
        type: probabilistic
        probabilistic:
          sampling_percentage: 1 # currently 1% for lower envs
```
If the collector is at 1% and your SDK is 5%, most traces will still be dropped.

observability-bot: Quick links — traces dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/trace-infra/celery-traces; collector config (internal): https://git.redwood.internal/infra/otel-collector/values.yaml

Jen L: I had similar missing-child-span issues — it ended up being that tasks weren't propagating context when celery beat/producer called apply_async. Make sure you're injecting headers on handoff: `propagator.inject(carrier=headers)` and the worker extracts them. If you call tasks outside HTTP request context, you need explicit propagation. :+1:

Sam H: Good call — our producer code uses apply_async(kwargs={}) but we weren't passing `headers`. I'll add propagation on enqueue. Also will try bumping sampler to 0.2 on a canary worker and enable debug logs (`OTEL_LOG_LEVEL=debug`) to surface exporter errors.

Olivia M: If you still don't see spans after those steps, post a trace id and I'll look it up in Tempo directly. Also verify that `service.name` is set consistently (worker vs web) — mismatch won't join traces in service-focused views but child spans still exist under the trace id.

Jen L: FYI I created SRE-512 to track follow-up (sampling audit + add flush on shutdown). Assigned to @Sam H and added a 15-min sync slot tomorrow 10:15 if needed.

Sam H: Thanks all — will try the init + propagation + sampler bump and report back in this thread. Appreciate the quick triage :eyes:
